system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
## Buyer review — Project Kestrel

**Basis:** AUD 24 million acquisition of 100% of Paperbark Analytics, debt-free/cash-free, NSW law. Recommendations below are buyer negotiating positions, not previously agreed terms. The underlying SPA and DD documents have not been provided, so their wording and current status require verification.

| Issue | Seller’s position | What the buyer should want | Recommendation and one-line reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001 — General liability cap** | General warranty liability capped at **20% / AUD 4.8m**. | A materially higher general cap, with separate treatment for protected categories. | **Counter at 50% / AUD 12m**, subject to diligence and recoverability; 20% leaves substantial acquisition risk with Buyer. |
| **SPA-N-002 — De minimis & basket** | Claims must exceed **AUD 25,000**; **AUD 250,000 deductible basket**, recovering only the excess. | Lower thresholds, a tipping basket and aggregation of related claims; exclusions for protected categories. | **Propose AUD 10,000 de minimis and AUD 100,000 tipping basket**, recovering qualifying claims from the first dollar once crossed; the Seller’s combination materially erodes recovery. |
| **SPA-N-003 — General claims time limit** | Notification within **18 months**; limitations apply to all Claims unless expressly excluded. | At least **24 months** for general warranties, separate category periods and preservation of timely notified claims. | **Counter at 24 months and reject universal application**; Buyer needs a meaningful operating and reporting cycle to identify issues. |
| **SPA-N-004 — Fundamental/Title regime** | Capacity and title subject to general caps and time limits. | Separate protection for capacity, ownership, authority and unencumbered transfer: no basket/de minimis, cap at least the price and longer survival. | **Require a separate regime: at least AUD 24m cap and six-year contractual claim window**, with execution and statutory limitation rules checked; defective ownership threatens the whole investment. |
| **SPA-N-005 — Fraud carve-out** | Limitations, exclusive remedies and non-reliance apply to all Claims; no express fraud exception is supplied. | Express preservation of fraud, fraudulent misrepresentation and fraudulent concealment claims and remedies. | **Carve fraud out of caps, thresholds, contractual time bars, disclosure/knowledge defences and remedy restrictions**, with appropriate attribution; Buyer should not contractually shield Seller fraud. |
| **SPA-N-006 — Disclosure scope** | Blanket disclosure of the data room, accounts, registers and public records. | Only fair disclosure with sufficient detail to identify the nature and scope of the exception, linked to relevant warranties. | **Reject blanket/deemed disclosure and require specific, indexed disclosures against an immutable room snapshot**; document availability is not adequate explanation of risk. |
| **SPA-N-007 — Buyer knowledge qualifier** | No claim for matters known by Buyer or advisers, including anything discoverable in the room or public records. | No knowledge defence; fallback limited to actual, conscious knowledge of named Buyer deal principals. | **Delete; if unavoidable, exclude constructive/imputed knowledge, adviser knowledge and any duty to investigate**, preserving agreed indemnities; discoverability would hollow out warranty protection. |
| **SPA-N-008 — Bluefen consent** | Reasonable endeavours; condition satisfied by written consent, although final consent and satisfaction of associated conditions are absent. | A Buyer-waivable completion condition requiring effective consent and satisfaction of clause 11.3 conditions without unacceptable changes. | **Do not complete until the consent and associated conditions are verified**, with a long-stop termination right; Bluefen represents approximately 30% of FY26 revenue. |
| **SPA-N-009 — Riverlark facility** | Approximately **AUD 3.2m** outstanding; security release after Completion. | Full repayment and effective discharge at Completion, supported by binding payout/release arrangements. | **Deduct debt through the agreed price mechanics and pay Riverlark directly under an agreed completion discharge process**; post-completion release exposes Buyer to inherited debt and security. |
| **SPA-N-010 — Employee bonuses** | Conditional **AUD 420,000** bonuses omitted from funds flow; on-costs unspecified. | Seller-funded bonuses and applicable payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs, with conditions and payment timing verified. | **Expressly allocate the liability to Seller and include it once in the funds flow/price adjustment, backed by an indemnity**; omission could leave Buyer funding transaction-triggered compensation. |
| **SPA-N-011 — Ironquay IP indemnity** | Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment; AUD 180,000 recorded open, without proof of payment or assignment. | Verified payment and complete IP transfer by Completion, plus protection for consequences of the existing title gap. | **Require cleared-payment evidence and confirmatory assignment; broaden the indemnity to ownership/use claims, defence costs and remediation**; paying an invoice alone may not resolve historic IP exposure. |
| **SPA-N-012 — Export/privacy incident** | Preliminary, expected immaterial; access, scope, notification duties and loss remain unresolved. | Prompt investigation, containment and legal assessment, compliance with applicable notification duties, and protection for pre-completion exposure. | **Require an incident workplan, information/consultation rights and a specific indemnity, with completion protection if findings are material**; uncertainty is neither proof of a breach nor a basis to dismiss the risk. |
| **SPA-N-013 — Sandbar renewals** | Three AUD 110,000 renewals, **AUD 330,000 aggregate**, characterised as ordinary-course costs. | Combined review of timing, scope, cancellation rights, accruals and commercial necessity. | **Assess the renewals together and restrict unapproved commitments; allocate through the correct price mechanism only if warranted**; neither ordinary-course status nor debt-like treatment is established. |
| **SPA-N-014 — Category separation** | General limitations, exclusive remedies and non-reliance extend to all Claims. | Expressly distinct rules for general warranties, fundamentals, tax, specific indemnities, price/debt adjustments, covenants and fraud. | **Replace catch-all limitations with an explicit category matrix and precedence clause**; otherwise general restrictions may defeat separately negotiated protections. |
| **SPA-N-015 — Title verification** | Relies on DD-012 share register recording Seller as 100% holder. | Independent verification of all issued shares, Seller ownership, encumbrances, options and other equity rights, plus effective transfer deliverables. | **Reconcile the register with corporate records, certificates and issuance/transfer history; obtain searches, releases and title warranties**; the register is important evidence, not complete verification of clean title. |
| **SPA-N-016 — Tax/IP open terms** | Tax and IP warranties treated as settled under the general regime. | Expressly open negotiations: a pre-completion tax indemnity with appropriate tax-specific periods and exclusions, and adequate IP ownership, licensing and infringement protection. | **Reject “settled” status and reserve tax/IP terms pending diligence**, including separate treatment where justified; the general regime does not adequately address latent tax or core-IP risks. |

**Immediate priorities:** secure Bluefen consent, Riverlark discharge and Ironquay title evidence; correct the bonus funds flow; and prevent blanket disclosure or all-Claims limitations from neutralising the negotiated protections.
=== END ADVICE ===
